seo_title: All {count} Blox Fruits Fish, Locations, Bait and Seas
meta_description: Compare Blox Fruits fish by catch status, location, bait, sea, and fish index, with notes for limited and unresolved catches.
intro_md: Fish are catches found across the three seas, from open water to named islands, ships, and Whirlpool routes. Their location and bait requirements decide whether a quick cast works or sends you sailing in circles with a very confident rod.
description_md:
## Plan the catch by sea and location

Start with the sea requirement. A catch that belongs to the Third Sea cannot become an early-game fishing target just because your rod feels optimistic. After that, check whether the fish can appear broadly or needs a named place such as an island, ship, castle, or Whirlpool.

Some fish have more than one valid location. Pick the one your character can reach safely and combine nearby targets into the same trip. This cuts down on sailing time and makes each bait loadout more useful.

## Match the bait to the fish

A named bait requirement is part of the route. Carnivore Bait, Abyssal Bait, Frozen Bait, and Epic Bait each appear on particular catches, so pack the listed option before leaving for the location. Showing up with the wrong bait is still a boat trip, just one with less fish.

When Bait says Any, the catch is not tied to one special bait in its recorded requirements. Location and sea can still narrow the route, so check all three facts together.

## Read catch status before spending time

Obtainable fish are the practical targets, but a few index entries still have incomplete catch details. If a location or method is not confirmed, do not invent a route from a similar-looking fish.

Limited or past event fish were tied to an earlier availability window. Unavailable or unresolved entries need current confirmation before you plan around them. Treat those statuses as a warning to check the live game, especially when an old seasonal catch looks ready to make a surprise return.
how_it_works_md: Status separates practical catches from limited or unresolved entries. Location, Bait, and Seas show the route requirements, while Fish index gives the catch's recorded index position.

description_json.Limited or past event: These catches were available through an earlier event period. Their return is not guaranteed outside a matching event.
description_json.Unavailable or unresolved: These index entries have unknown catch details or availability that still needs confirmation. Do not plan a fishing route around them yet.

faq_json.q: How do I choose where to catch a fish in Blox Fruits?
faq_json.a: Check its sea first, then its location. A named island, ship, castle, or Whirlpool narrows the route, while Any is not tied to one named location in the recorded requirements.

faq_json.q: Do all Blox Fruits fish need special bait?
faq_json.a: No. Some catches name Carnivore, Abyssal, Frozen, or Epic Bait, while others show Any. Always pair the bait field with the listed location and sea.

faq_json.q: Can I catch a limited or past event fish now?
faq_json.a: Do not assume it is active. These catches belonged to an earlier availability window, so confirm that the matching event has returned before spending time on the route.

faq_json.q: What does unavailable or unresolved mean for a fish?
faq_json.a: Its current availability or exact catch method is not confirmed. Wait for a clear in-game route instead of copying the location or bait from another fish.
It is the catch's recorded position in the fishing index. It is an identifier, not a power or rarity ranking.

wiki_md: Fish are catches made with fishing gear across the First, Second, and Third Sea. Some can appear broadly, while others send you to places such as the Sea of Treats, Cursed Ship, or Whirlpool and may call for a named bait. Checking the sea, location, and bait keeps a fishing trip from becoming a scenic boat ride with no fish.
